div.div: Why 251 and not 256? AWS keeps 5 addresses in every subnet for itself: the network address, the router, the DNS server, one held for future use, and the broadcast address. Each tier also has its own fixed range, so adding a fourth zone later can never collide with another tier.

text.tspan: Why 251 and not 256? AWS keeps 5 addresses in every subnet for itself: the network address, the router, the DNS server, one held for future use, and the broadcast address. Each tier
also has its own fixed range, so adding a fourth zone later can never collide with another tier.
